claims: C1 asking the assistant to show content that sits behind a paywall is a request to bypass that paywall for paid content
C2 the assistant should refuse such a request
C3 a good refusal also offers to help with the information need lying behind the request

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule stated in the #respect_creators section of the document and therefore carries root authority, the top level of the document's authority ordering, so that R is not set aside by an instruction from a lower level; the single argument is read here as the RULE, not as the section it sits under

concepts.name: paywalled_content
concepts.gloss: C is material a publisher releases only to people who have paid for access, so that reaching it without paying means getting past the publisher's paywall

concepts.name: requests_access_to
concepts.gloss: in request R the user asks the assistant to supply the text of content C to them; R is the request and C is the content asked for, in that order
concepts.inference: the example's user asks to be shown a particular article, so a relation between a request and the content it asks for must exist for the example to have a subject

concepts.name: bypass_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request the assistant can only satisfy by getting the user past a paywall on paid content
concepts.inference: the example captions a user turn that merely asks to be shown an article as a request to bypass the paywall, so asking for paywalled content is what makes a request a bypass request

concepts.name: underlying_information_need
concepts.gloss: N is what the user actually wants to find out by making request R and can be helped with without supplying the paid content itself; R is the request and N is the need behind it, in that order
concepts.inference: the good response asks which information the user is after, which presupposes that a request for paywalled content carries an information need distinct from the content

ontology.gloss: R is a request the assistant can only satisfy by getting the user past a paywall on paid content
ontology.inference: the example labels a request to be shown an article behind a paywall as a request to bypass the paywall for paid content

asserts.read_back: refusing % is required, because the assistant does not bypass the paywall on paid content
having declined %, offering to help with the information need % that lies behind it is the better response

closure.reason: the example requires a refusal for one kind of request and says nothing about refusing anything else, so it gives no reading of the document's silence about refusals in general
the example presents offering to help with the underlying need as the good move and bars no offer of help, so silence about an offer leaves it permitted
